_skill.name: lap_annotation
_skill.description: Per-label telemetry characteristics for the behavior parent labels (O, OD, PS, RM, MSP, MSR) that every saved lap segment must contain at least one of. EA remains documented as clean driving context, but it is not a substitute for the required behavior parent set in this flow. Each label declares its telemetry signature (driver/expert trajectory evidence, expert_time_difference slope, brake overlap, opponent context, etc.) and the global_rules_by_session blocks prescribe the detection procedure. Source of truth for "does this range qualify as MSP / RM / O / OD / MSR / PS ... at all?" The circuit + circuit_section labels are picked by the LLM via the `get_circuit_id` / `locate_circuit_section` tools (geometry from `app/shared/circuit_sections.py`). Solo sessions are split by circuit section; sessions with opponent data emit only close overtake offence / defense engagement windows.
when_to_use: Lap excerpter assigning one parent label per circuit section.
Building the system prompt for the lap-flow planner/synthesizer.
Evaluator checks for parent-label justification against telemetry.

action_model.parent_segment: A saved lap parent segment is a group of one or more complete driving actions that together justify the behavior parent label over the final iloc range. It is not an arbitrary graph slice, a single apex moment, or one isolated label symptom.
action_model.action: An action is a coherent driver/expert maneuver over an iloc interval, evaluated through the related turning / trajectory, throttle input, and brake input for that same interval. Turning may be straight, constant, increasing, or unwinding; throttle and brake may be applied, released, modulated, held steady, or intentionally zero.
action_model.child_segment: Detailed child sub-segments may isolate a smaller action or phase for sub-labels, but the lap parent segment remains the action group that gives the parent behavior its context.

EA.name: Expert Adherence (Training)
EA.characteristics:
Player matches or cleanly outperforms the expert through the section.
  - Standard adherence: the driver line stays close to the expert racing line for the whole range, `expert_time_difference` is stable, and speed delta at sampled ilocs is small.
  - A time gap below 200ms is not a mistake by itself. When `expert_time_difference` exists and the absolute gap or gap change remains under 200ms with no off-track/cutting/instability or new technical-error evidence, categorize the section as EA.
  - Expert-or-better clean section: EA can still apply when the player is ahead of the expert, gaining on the expert, or using a cleaner/faster line than the expert, even if the line is wider/tighter than the expert reference. Require no off-track/cutting/instability evidence and no MSP / RM / MSR / PS gate.
  - When `expert_time_difference` exists, confirm with `find_trend_runs` and `compute_slope`. Use deterministic trend verdict fields; a positive but flat time gap only means the player is already behind, not that a new mistake happened inside this range.
  - When `expert_time_difference` is absent, do not rule out EA solely because the slope gate is unavailable. Use trajectory, speed/brake/throttle samples, segment shape, and the absence of MSP/RM/MSR/PS evidence; note that MSP/RM slope gates cannot be satisfied.
Mutually exclusive with MSP and RM.

MSP.name: Mistake (Practice)
MSP.characteristics:
Technical driving error causing time loss or instability, NOT caused by interaction with a close opponent.
  - MSP / RM boundary is decided by whether a new mistake action or newly worsening loss rate happens inside this split section, not by the section's start iloc or by `expert_time_difference` starting near zero. At lap/session start, near-zero time difference is baseline context only.
  - If the section contains the new mistake action (run wide, cut tight, braking / throttle error, instability, or newly worsening time-loss rate), label the section MSP even if the driver later recovers, merges back, or the whole-section loss-rate slope decreases.
  - `expert_time_difference` must show a new or worsening time-loss event inside the range. Confirm with `find_trend_runs` and `compute_slope`: a rising time-gap run means the player is losing time, but it is MSP only when the loss rate itself strengthens inside this section or increases beyond the already-carried incoming slope and the absolute gap or gap change is at least 200ms. Do not infer MSP from a time gap below 200ms, absolute gap growth, endpoint delta, `starts_near_zero`, or `total_change_direction` alone. If the graph enters the section already rising and then the whole-section slope shape decreases or reverses while trajectory/brake/throttle evidence shows merge-back behavior, treat that as recovery from a prior mistake, not a new MSP.
  - Do not use speed or speed delta as the deciding evidence for MSP vs RM; speed is too fuzzy for the practice parent-label boundary. Use trajectory, brake/throttle action, and deterministic time-difference trend verdicts instead.
  - Use `compute_slope` as the whole-range summary only after localizing the action. If its whole-section slope-shape field shows `slope_shape` as `slope_decreasing_over_section` or `reversing_to_falling_within_section`, or local trend runs show falling/flat recovery, decide whether the earlier part is a new mistake action or a carried prior loss; do not relabel carried recovery as MSP solely because total change is rising.
  - The driver line exceeds the expert envelope because of a new in-section spike outward (ran wide) or inward (cut tight). Recovery back toward the expert racing line later in the same section does not cancel MSP when the section began with the mistake action, but a range that begins after the mistake and primarily merges back is RM.
  - Use RM instead when the section does not contain the new mistake action and the first qualifying action is recovery / merge from an already-carried off-line state, off-track state, instability, or prior incident.
  - In opponent-capable data, `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`
    does NOT return an adverse racing outcome (`failed_attack` or
    `broken_defense`). A close opponent + adverse classifier outcome ⇒ MSR.
Mutually exclusive with EA, RM, MSR. The detailed-annotation flow refines MSP sub-ranges later — attach MSP at the section level when the section starts with or is dominated by a technical error that occurs inside the section.

MSR.name: Mistake (Racing)
MSR.characteristics:
Time / position loss caused by an interaction with a close opponent inside the section.
  - Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require
    `outcome` = `failed_attack` or `broken_defense` with medium/high
    confidence. Low / weak confidence means inspect opponent trajectory
    or submit an empty label list.
  - Use `find_nearest_opponent` / `query_opponent_trajectory` only as
    supporting evidence for the primary slot and technique.
  - `expert_time_difference` typically grows across the
    interaction window.
Mutually exclusive with EA, RM, MSP. No close opponent or classifier outcome not in {failed_attack, broken_defense} ⇒ not MSR.

RM.name: Recovery & Merge
RM.characteristics:
Player recovering from a prior mistake inside this section.
  - RM / MSP boundary is decided by whether the current split section contains the new mistake action. Use RM when the section does not contain the new mistake action and the first qualifying behavior is recovery / merge from an already-carried off-line state, off-track state, instability, prior incident, or already-rising expert-time gap.
  - A preceding mistake/off-track/incident explains why recovery is needed. An `expert_time_difference` trace that enters the range already rising is evidence that time loss may have begun before this section; do not treat that incoming positive slope as a new in-section MSP by itself. A near-zero starting value is also not MSP evidence by itself, especially at lap/session start.
  - `expert_time_difference` should show recovery pressure inside the range. A falling `find_trend_runs` recovery run is recovery evidence. Also accept a rising whole-range gap when `compute_slope` reports whole-section recovery shape (`slope_shape` as `slope_decreasing_over_section` or `reversing_to_falling_within_section`) and the action evidence shows recovery / merge.
  - The driver line trends back toward the expert racing line from a non-zero or already-compromised state, with brake/throttle action consistent with rejoining or merging back. This merge-back action is RM even if the absolute `expert_time_difference` gap is still growing across the whole range.
  - Do not use speed or speed delta as the deciding evidence for RM vs MSP; speed is too fuzzy for the practice parent-label boundary.
Do NOT use RM just because an MSP section has a later recovery phase; if the section starts with a mistake action that occurs in this section, the whole parent segment is MSP and recovery is described in the reasoning or detailed child sub-segment. Do NOT attach when the player started clean with no carried mistake/off-line state — that's EA or an empty parent, not RM. Mutually exclusive with EA and MSP.

PS.name: Pit Stop
PS.characteristics:
Player is in the circuit's Pit section. Pit procedure is PS even when the car is accelerating out and returning toward the racing surface.
  - Require pit evidence from a `locate_circuit_section` result that overlaps the circuit's known Pit section.
  - When `locate_circuit_section` is ambiguous between Pit and the adjacent straight because they share a normalized range, a sustained pit-lane-style trajectory offset plus large player/expert speed separation or slow pit-exit acceleration is sufficient Pit-section procedure evidence.
  - Do not label PS from speed rise, low speed, trajectory offset, or acceleration back toward track speed alone when the range is in a normal racing section away from Pit.
Compatible with the circuit label. Do NOT combine with EA / MSP / MSR / O / OD.

O.name: Successful Overtake
O.characteristics:
Player gained a position on a specific opponent inside the section. Multi-car positional data (`Car_{1..60}_pos_{x,y,z}`) is the gate.
  - Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require
    `outcome: pass_completed` with medium/high confidence — the
    deterministic signed longitudinal relationship says the opponent
    was ahead at entry and behind by exit. Empty / no-data / non-pass
    outcomes ⇒ do NOT attach O. Low / weak confidence means inspect opponent
    trajectory or submit an empty label list.
  - Player-trace evidence to ALSO hold: late-brake signature
    past the expert reference, sustained outside / inside line
    deviation NOT explained by MSP / RM, or speed > expert on
    equal-or-less throttle (draft).
A close opponent + failed attack is MSR at the section level — sub-labelled `MSR1` in the detailed flow. A successful defense is OD, not O.

OD.name: Successful Defense
OD.characteristics:
Player held position against a real, close opponent inside the section.
  - Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require
    `outcome: held_defense` with medium/high confidence — the
    deterministic relationship says the opponent threatened from behind
    / alongside but did not get ahead by exit. A merely close car with no
    held-defense outcome is not OD. Low / weak confidence means inspect opponent
    trajectory or submit an empty label list.
  - Player-trace evidence to ALSO hold: brake initiation
    earlier than expert and/or trajectory tighter than expert
    (inside cover), or a throttle lift on a straight with no
    brake onset (defensive lift). Time delta need not be flat
    — it may grow briefly during the defense as long as the
    position holds.
A defense that failed (opponent got past) is MSR at the section level — sub-labelled `MSR2` in the detailed flow.

practice: Solo sessions are processed as normal driving sections split by circuit section.
Only practice-session behavior parents {PS, RM, MSP} are eligible. Do not evaluate or attach racing-session behavior parents O / OD / MSR in practice mode.

Pick MSP for a technical driving mistake, RM for recovery from a prior mistake, or PS for Pit-section procedure. For MSP vs RM, classify by whether the mistake action or worsening loss-rate slope occurs inside the split section: new mistake action / strengthening loss-rate slope => MSP even if recovery/merge happens later; no new mistake action and the first qualifying action is recovery/merge from carried offset, instability, or prior time loss => RM.

Use `find_trend_runs` and `compute_slope` on `expert_time_difference` for time-loss / recovery evidence. Do not use the section's start index, `starts_near_zero`, absolute endpoint gap, or total endpoint delta as MSP evidence by itself. A time gap below 200ms is not a mistake; when the rest of the section is clean, categorize it as EA. A constant carried gap is not a new mistake or recovery.
Use deterministic trajectory queries for peak deviation plus returned near-line summary (`near_zero_fraction`, `starts_near_zero`, `ends_near_zero`, `moves_toward_zero`).
Driver/expert turning / trajectory, brake, and throttle comparison is required for segment completeness at entry or exit, not only for sub-labels.
racing: Sessions with opponent data are processed only as close overtake offence / defense engagement windows.
Only racing-session behavior parents {O, OD, MSR, PS} are eligible. Do not evaluate or attach practice-session behavior parents MSP / RM in racing mode.
Pick O for a successful attacking pass, OD for a held defense, or MSR for a failed attack / broken defense.

The deterministic interaction evidence for O / OD / MSR is `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)` over the full current range: O requires `outcome: pass_completed`; OD requires `outcome: held_defense`; MSR requires `outcome` in {`failed_attack`, `broken_defense`}.
Prefer labels only when the classifier confidence is medium/high. Low / weak classifier confidence means inspect `query_opponent_trajectory` or submit an empty label list if evidence remains unclear.

The classifier uses expert-trajectory projection for signed longitudinal / lateral gaps when expert positions exist, and reports `coordinate_frame` so cite whether it used `expert_path_projection` or `player_heading_projection`.
If the classifier does not support a required O / OD / MSR outcome, submit an empty label list rather than labeling normal practice-driving telemetry.
PS remains eligible in racing mode only for Pit-section procedure with pit evidence; do not use it for ordinary opponent interactions or combine it with O / OD / MSR.
Use `find_nearest_opponent` and `query_opponent_trajectory(start, end, slot, n_samples)` for supporting primary-slot details and technique.
common: Every saved lap segment must include at least one eligible behavior parent label. Circuit labels, circuit_section labels, segment-type labels, sub-labels, and EA do not satisfy this requirement.
If no eligible behavior parent fits the whole split-section range, submit `label_ids: []` to drop the range; do not save a segment with only circuit / section / segment-type / sub-label / EA labels.
Call `get_circuit_id` and `locate_circuit_section` for circuit context. Include circuit / circuit_section ids only when an eligible behavior parent is also included.

When `locate_circuit_section` reports `is_ambiguous`, use `top_matches` as competing evidence and choose exactly one circuit_section id. For Pit-vs-straight ties, choose Pit when Pit-section evidence supports pit procedure; otherwise choose the normal racing-surface section.

Whole-range label rule: every behavior, segment-type, and sub-label must describe the final annotation range as a whole. Do not attach a label because it matches only one phase, one apex moment, or a short slice inside the range; omit that label or leave it for detailed child sub-segment annotation.

Segment model: a saved lap parent segment is a group of one or more complete driving actions that together justify the behavior parent label over the final iloc range; it is not an arbitrary graph slice, a single apex moment, or one isolated label symptom.

Action model: each action must be evaluated as the related turning / trajectory, throttle input, and brake input over the same iloc interval. Zero or steady throttle / brake still count as input states when they explain the action.

Segment completeness rule: the parent segment must keep the complete action group needed for the chosen behavior parent. Do not clip the turning, throttle, or brake portion that makes the action understandable.

For entry actions, include the relevant turn-in / entry trajectory plus the complete brake action made by the driver and the comparable expert brake action: first relevant application / onset before turn-in through brake release / end of braking or the stable post-brake transition.

For exit actions, include the relevant exit / unwind trajectory plus the complete throttle action made by the driver and the comparable expert throttle action: first relevant reapplication or lift point through the stabilized exit / full-throttle state.

Before scoring the final parent label, identify the complete action or action group inside the proposed parent segment and cite the turning / trajectory, throttle, and brake evidence that makes it complete.

Bounds must come from these knowledge-base rules plus deterministic tool results over `Physics_brake` / `Physics_gas` and `expert_optimal_brake` / `expert_optimal_throttle`; do not substitute remembered conventions, graph-only guesses, or arbitrary padding.
If deterministic results do not establish the full action interval inside the split-section range, submit `label_ids: []` rather than saving an incomplete parent segment.

Render diagnostic graphs needed for the eligible labels. For MSP / RM parent selection, use trajectory evidence, `expert_time_difference`, brake / throttle, and deterministic telemetry queries as evidence; do not use speed or speed delta as the deciding evidence for the practice parent-label boundary.
Use `find_trend_runs` on `expert_time_difference` and cite returned `verdict`, `selected_losing_time_run`, and `selected_recovery_run` to localize gap growth or shrinkage.
Use `compute_slope` on `expert_time_difference` and cite returned `unit`, `delta_value`, `total_change_direction`, `slope_shape` only as the whole-range summary after checking local trend runs.

Never invent math adjectives from the raw slope number; deterministic tool verdict fields are the source of truth for units, local time-loss/recovery runs, whole-section slope-shape trend, and parent-segment action bounds.

If the picked main label, segment-type label, or sub-label fits only part of the split-section range, the engagement starts before the range, the pass resolves after the range, an entry brake action or exit throttle action would be clipped, or classifier confidence is low / weak, omit that label or submit `label_ids: []`.
Optionally pick segment-type labels when the base segment shape or corner-shape refinement is unambiguous and the returned catalog metadata has `lap_parent_allowed: true`.

Use `measure_segment_shape` as the deterministic segment-shape summary. Add a corner-shape refinement only when `measure_segment_shape.corner_shape_refinement.shape_key` matches that label's `shape_key` for the final range; non-empty `phases` alone is not enough.
ST10 Hairpin requires `measure_segment_shape.corner_shape_refinement` to report the required hairpin gate flag true: `is_near_u_turn`.

Entry/apex/exit altitude labels have `annotation_scope: subsegment_only` and `lap_parent_allowed: false`; they describe separate corner-phase subsegments, not a single lap parent segment covering the whole corner. Their uphill / level / downhill trend must come from `measure_segment_shape.altitude.<phase>.slope_angle_degrees` and `trend`, not raw height difference alone.

Submit `label_ids` plus a 4-6 sentence `reasoning` note citing deterministic verdict fields plus ilocs / values / offset peaks / classifier outcome / confidence level / opponent slot fields, as applicable.
Never invent label IDs. Use only IDs from the eligible behavior list, circuit / section capability results, or label catalog search results.
Empty `label_ids` `[]` is the valid drop-this-section signal, not a saved annotation without a required behavior parent.
Final iloc range is the split-section range and must be at least 3 ilocs.

global_rules: Compatibility note: session-specific lap detection policy lives in `lap_annotation.global_rules_by_session.practice`, `lap_annotation.global_rules_by_session.racing`, and `lap_annotation.global_rules_by_session.common`. Render the detected session mode plus common rules instead of this legacy key.
